title: Research sprint goal: Research: CPU-only text analysis, rules as data and self-hosted observability for a corpus service
goal: The sprint goal's open questions are answered from official sources (project docs, model cards, repositories; kb tools first, live docs for the gaps) and written as kb facts and gap entries through the kb skills. Open (pack coverage none, weak or a false good, 2026-10-11): (1) spaCy pinned to one patch, a pipeline packaged as a wheel (spacy package) in a private registry, the meta's spacy_version range and a stamp of its inputs; (2) Morfeusz 2 for Polish as lemma authority: dictionaries, licence, Python binding, and the degraded arm without it (spaCy's Polish lemmatizer); (3) ONNX Runtime CPU inference in Rust via the ort crate: version pinning, download or load-dynamic, the cargo features that enable GPU providers and how a build refuses them, model artifacts pinned by hash with licence fields; (4) GLiNER as a general zero-shot NER library (multilingual models, licences, CPU and ONNX) and GLiREL for zero-shot relations; (5) MMLW-e5 Polish sentence embeddings (dimensions, licence, query and passage prefixes); (6) coreference resolution options; (7) Datalog engines embeddable in Rust (Crepe, Ascent, Datafrog) for closure and contradiction rules; (8) Oxigraph as an embedded read-only RDF store with named graphs and SPARQL 1.1; (9) GoRules JSON Decision Model and zen-engine: node kinds, refusing function (JavaScript) nodes, versioning by effective date; (10) Fluent in Rust (fluent-rs) and TypeScript (@fluent/bundle), typed accessors, a lint of literals; (11) content-addressed ids and JSON Lines; (12) OpenTelemetry Collector with OTLP, Prometheus retention and /metrics exposition, Loki and Tempo retention, Grafana, JSON logs to stdout. Already answered: pgvector operators and licence (agents/hybrid-retrieval.md), Fluent Python runtime and FTL syntax (arch/texts-catalogue-formats.md), en_core_web_lg licence (privacy/spacy-model-licence.md), GLiNER PII cards (privacy/gliner-models.md).
